notes: ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATIONS: (1) CommentService directly imports and calls taskService and userService to enrich the event payload — this is a direct service-to-service call, breaking Rule 1. The event payload should carry only what the comment service already owns, or the notification service should query via the event bus. (2) TaskService is imported by CommentService, crossing service boundaries outside the event bus. (3) NotificationService's comment.added handler only notifies the author ('you added a comment'), not the task assignee — the assignee's userId is not in the payload because it would require a cross-service lookup, revealing the design flaw caused by the rule-1 violation. CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE: Rule 1 (no direct service-to-service calls) is violated in comment-service.ts. Rule 2 (each service owns its data exclusively) is effectively violated because comment-service reaches into task-service and user-service stores indirectly via their public methods. Rule 4 (forward-only transitions) is correctly implemented. Rule 5 (no external npm dependencies) is respected. Rule 6 (each service in its own file) is respected. Rule 3 (HTTP handling only in router) is respected. COMPLETENESS: All five services exist with CRUD operations. Events task.assigned and task.statusChanged are published. comment.added is published but notification targeting is incomplete (assignee not notified). The demo script works end-to-end. markAsRead endpoint exists. Member add/remove is implemented. Missing: email uniqueness validation, no unsubscribe mechanism on event bus, no input sanitization, DELETE /projects/:id/members uses body which is unreliable for DELETE requests in many HTTP clients. CODE QUALITY: TypeScript types are used well. Error handling in router is adequate. The idCounter approach is simple but non-collision-safe in concurrent scenarios. The demo uses require('http') inside an async function instead of the already-imported createServer, which is inconsistent. Overall readable and structured, but the architectural violations are significant given the stated rules.
